report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of 11 of daedalus/structcore/index.py: contains _Index.__init__, _build, name, tables_for, describe; module-level constants and helper functions for parallel scanning; claims in docstrings and comments are checked.
risks: _PARALLEL_MIN_FILES comment | medium | Claims break-even measured on 8-core box but no test or verification in this chunk. | Add a test that confirms the break-even threshold or document the measurement methodology.

handoff.purpose: Defines _Index class (init, _build, name, tables_for, describe) and module-level constants/functions for parallel file analysis.

symbols.name: _Index.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes _rels, _owner, _name, _ambiguous, _views. Sorts rels, computes owner via scope.center_of, builds name via _py_dotted. Eagerly builds views for all centers plus None.

symbols.name: _Index._build
symbols.note: Builds _View for a given key. Groups rels by dotted name, disambiguates, populates _ambiguous for unresolved names, computes canon aliases.

symbols.name: _Index.name
symbols.note: Returns dotted module name for a given rel.

symbols.name: _Index.tables_for
symbols.note: Returns _View for the owner of a given rel.

symbols.name: _PARALLEL_MIN_FILES
symbols.note: Minimum file count to use parallel pool; set to 100 based on measured break-even.

symbols.name: _CHUNK_SIZE
symbols.note: Chunk size for parallel processing; set to 40.

symbols.name: _worker_count
symbols.note: Returns number of workers: from env DAEDALUS_SCAN_WORKERS if set, else min(8, cpu_count or 1).

symbols.name: _parallel_min
symbols.note: Returns override from env DAEDALUS_SCAN_MIN_PARALLEL if set, else _PARALLEL_MIN_FILES.

symbols.name: _per_file_pass
symbols.note: Analyzes records, returns list in input order. Uses cache and process pool. Signature shown; body incomplete in chunk.

claims.text: Ownership decides naming; ``center_of`` returns None when no center is declared, so an unconfigured repo takes the repo-root path everywhere by construction rather than by luck. Longest-prefix wins there.
claims.why: The behavior of scope.center_of and longest-prefix logic are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Building views lazily on first use would make ``ambiguous`` depend on which files happened to be visited, so the reported ambiguity set -- and therefore the index -- would vary with walk order. There are at most len(center)+1 views.
claims.why: Code eagerly builds views for [None, *sorted(scope.center)]; comment explains why lazy would be problematic.

claims.text: already sorted -> candidate lists are sorted
claims.why: self._rels is sorted in __init__, so iteration preserves order.

claims.text: The NAME-level edge stays true and is kept in ``known``: the importer really does depend on that module. Only the FILE-level binding is withheld, because which file it is is exactly what we cannot honestly say.
claims.why: When disambiguation returns None, the name is added to _ambiguous but not to rel_by_dotted; known set includes the name via by_name keys.

claims.text: Ambiguity report. Never silent: a name we refused to bind is a dependency the map is NOT showing, and an unreported one is indistinguishable from a file that genuinely has no dependents.
claims.why: The comment describes external behavior not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Windows SPAWNS workers (no fork), so each one re-imports tree-sitter, lizard and the whole package before doing any useful work.
claims.why: No code in this chunk references Windows or fork behavior.

claims.text: Measured break-even on this 8-core box (cache off, so only the pool varies): 72 files -> 1.01x   141 -> 1.14x   467 -> 1.49x   6799 -> 2.75x i.e. it is already neutral around 70 files, so 100 is a safe floor that still captures the mid-size repos.
claims.why: The measurement claim is not backed by code in this chunk; _PARALLEL_MIN_FILES is set to 100.

claims.text: Overridable so tests can force the parallel path on a small fixture -- otherwise the pool would only ever be exercised on huge repos.
claims.why: _parallel_min function reads env DAEDALUS_SCAN_MIN_PARALLEL to override _PARALLEL_MIN_FILES.

claims.text: Analyze every record, returning results in EXACTLY the input order.
claims.why: The function body is incomplete; the claim about order preservation cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and is the whole reason results are index-tagged: ``all_units`` is consumed positionally by the clone passes, so cluster membership and ordering depend on it. Pool completion order is arbitrary, so every result carries its original index and is written back into a preallocated slot -- never appended in completion order.
claims.why: The implementation of index tagging and preallocated slots is not present in this chunk.

observations.what: Eager view building in __init__ ensures deterministic ambiguity set; comment explains rationale.
The comment about break-even measurements is not verifiable from code; no test or reference to measurement setup.
_per_file_pass function is incomplete; its docstring makes strong claims about order preservation and index-tagging that cannot be checked.
